html:
A king of Ethiopia from the Zagwe dynasty who reigned from about 1181 to 1221. He is famous for the churches cut down into solid rock in the town that now bears his name.

The Zagwe came from the Agaw people and ruled the Christian highlands after the decline of Aksum. Their capital was Roha, in the mountains of Lasta. Legend says that when Lalibela was born a swarm of bees surrounded him, which his mother took as a sign that he would rule. His name is said to mean "the bees recognise his sovereignty".

Tradition says he set out to build a new Jerusalem in Ethiopia, perhaps after Saladin took the real one in 1187 and made pilgrimage harder. The rock-hewn churches were carved in his time, and the town was renamed in his honour. Pious stories say angels worked on them at night.

The Ethiopian church honours Lalibela as a saint. Later in the 13th century the Zagwe were overthrown by a dynasty claiming descent from Solomon, which founded the Ethiopian Empire that lasted until 1974.
